summary: The text argues for preserving the E-Rate program to maintain broadband access for libraries and schools, citing its importance for community programs and educational outcomes. It opposes any efforts to sunset or restrict the program, emphasizing the cost and equity implications of doing so.

claims.argument: Preserving E-Rate ensures continued broadband access for libraries and schools, supporting community programs and educational outcomes
claims.evidence_quote: It is vital to preserve the E-Rate program, to continue helping public libraries and schools across the state provide technology access by upgrading broadband capacity and internet speeds, paying ongoing internet access costs, modernizing wiring and internal network infrastructure, and expanding public Wi-Fi access.
